analysis.investment_thesis: Allied Blenders grew revenue at just 3.3% CAGR over five years while generating near-zero profits (INR 1–3 Cr annually from FY21–FY24) — and now trades at 59.8x P/E on a suspicious single-year profit of INR 195 Cr following an IPO-related equity infusion. At this valuation with this track record, the risk-reward is deeply unfavourable.
key_strengths: Officer's Choice is a genuinely recognised brand — India's largest selling whisky by volume — providing some pricing power
Promoter holding at 80.91% is strong — full skin in the game and no dilution concerns
ROCE of 21.1% and ROE of 20% in FY25 look attractive — but these must be viewed with extreme scepticism given the massive equity base change
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 3.3% over 5 years in a consumer staples category — this is a stagnant top line, not a compounder

FY25 net profit of INR 195 Cr is implausible given years of INR 1–3 Cr profits; the equity base quintupled (INR 407 Cr → INR 1,558 Cr) in one year suggesting IPO proceeds are distorting returns metrics
State government taxation and regulatory risk make alcohol a structurally difficult business — margins are thin (11.69%) and pricing is not fully in the company's control
red_flags: Operating cash flow turned sharply negative in FY25 (-INR 678 Cr) after being consistently positive — the year profits spiked, OCF collapsed — a classic red flag
P/E of 59.8x (forward 47x) for a business with near-zero historical earnings and 3.3% revenue growth is speculative, not value investing
Net profit of INR 1–3 Cr for FY21–FY24 despite INR 3,000+ Cr revenue means the business was barely surviving operationally — the brand strength was not translating to shareholder value
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I built DMart on the principle that a good business generates predictable, growing cash profits year after year. Allied Blenders fails this test completely — for four consecutive years (FY21–FY24) it reported INR 1–3 Cr of net profit on INR 2,300–3,300 Cr of revenue, a profit margin of essentially zero. The sudden jump to INR 195 Cr in FY25 coincides with the equity base expanding from INR 407 Cr to INR 1,558 Cr (likely IPO proceeds), which makes ROE and ROCE metrics meaningless for this year.

The alcohol business in India is structurally challenged — state excise duties, price controls in many markets, and distribution restrictions all cap the upside. Officer's Choice is a high-volume, low-margin product. At 59.8x P/E with a 3.3% revenue CAGR, the market is paying a luxury brand multiple for a commodity blended spirits company. I see no margin of safety here and would not touch this stock.
